premises.scope: For every fixed symmetric A, the optimal interval-density height over arbitrary independent cap-one marginals equals the optimum over indicator densities of bounded finite unions of intervals of total length one; no uniform complexity bound.
Literal B_*=I-(2/3)11^T anchor block with arbitrary outside couplings/curvature and translations has essential density cap 6 sqrt(pi); outside localization is mass-linear.

result.statement: For every fixed symmetric A and p in (0,1), the optimal homogeneous QFORM concentration height over all independent cap-one marginals equals the supremum over p-centered indicator laws of bounded finite unions of total length one and affine coefficients b in Range(A) of D(L(Y^T A Y+b^T Y)). The identity is exact including +infinity. Taking the supremum over all target A preserves the full universal constant.
result.proof_key: Translate each finite-union extreme marginal by its lower p-quantile m_i; X^TAX=Y^TAY+2(Am)^TY+m^TAm. Conversely every b in Range(A) equals 2Am. Output scalar shifts do not change concentration height.

partner_application.inequality: For mathcal A=[[B_*,C],[C^T,D]], centered finite-union product inputs and every b in Range(mathcal A) satisfy ||p_{Y^T mathcal A Y+b^T Y}||_infty,ess <= 6 sqrt(pi).

unresolved_implication: Prove a whole-law density receiver on the centered finite-union extreme core, uniform in fragment count, support diameter and fragment locations, from only s_3(A)>=1, without paying a tiny physical principal minor.
suggested_next_step: Use the centered finite-union core as the legal input endpoint for grouped-bank / product-preserving spectral extraction; do not spend further runs on truncation or centering unless a new correction invalidates the source theorem.
